title: Everyday Urban U1 pre-ride check
summary: A compact check of tires, wheels, brakes, cockpit and utility hardware before daily riding.

steps.title: Inspect tires and wheels
steps.instruction: Check both tires for visible damage and measure pressure against the actual tire/rim/bicycle guidance. Spin each wheel and look for obvious wobble, rubbing or poor seating.
steps.why: The tires and wheels carry the bicycle and create the contact patches used for steering and braking.
steps.warning: Do not ride a tire with structural casing damage, an unexplained bulge or visibly unsafe seating.
steps.check: Both tires and wheels appear serviceable and pressures are within the actual system limits.

steps.title: Check braking response
steps.instruction: Operate both brakes while stationary, then verify during a controlled low-speed roll that braking feels predictable and neither wheel shows abnormal rubbing or brake behavior.
steps.why: Daily utility equipment is only useful if the bicycle can be controlled and stopped predictably.
steps.warning: If braking is weak, inconsistent, leaking, heavily rubbing or otherwise abnormal, stop and identify the cause before normal riding.
steps.check: Both brakes respond predictably in a controlled check.

steps.title: Confirm steering and contact points
steps.instruction: Check that the handlebar, grips, saddle and pedals do not show obvious looseness, damage or unintended movement.
steps.why: Loose rider-control components can turn a normal city maneuver into a loss of control.
steps.warning: Do not tighten cockpit or seat hardware by guesswork; use the component-specific procedure and torque specification.
steps.check: Visible control/contact components appear secure and undamaged.

steps.title: Check the hardware you rely on today
steps.instruction: Inspect the rack, fenders, lights and kickstand for obvious looseness, interference or damage. Confirm the lights you intend to use operate normally.
steps.why: Utility accessories sit close to moving wheels and are used repeatedly, so looseness or interference deserves attention before riding.
steps.warning: If a rack, fender or stand can contact a wheel or interfere with controls, do not ride until the fault is corrected.
steps.check: Required utility hardware is secure enough for the intended ride and does not interfere with moving parts.
